claims.text: Increasing Cr and/or Al concentration in a single-phase HEA drives preferential segregation of those elements to the surface during high-temperature exposure.
Preferential surface segregation of Cr and/or Al produces a reactive-element-enriched region at the oxide/alloy interface.
Sluggish diffusion is a characteristic high-temperature kinetic effect in multi-element HEA matrices.
Sluggish matrix diffusion combined with a concentration gradient promotes selective Cr/Al segregation to the surface.
Cr/Al enrichment enables rapid nucleation and growth of a protective oxide scale.
The resulting oxide scale is compact, continuous, adherent, and self-healing.
The compact oxide scale acts as a diffusion barrier against further oxidation.
AlCoCrFeNi can serve as a homogenized, single-phase initial HEA for the proposed comparison.
Increasing Cr/Al concentration relative to a lower-content baseline will produce a thinner oxide layer.
Increasing Cr/Al concentration will produce a more uniform and adherent oxide layer.
Increasing Cr/Al concentration will reduce oxidation mass gain relative to the baseline.
In-situ surface analysis will detect significant Cr/Al enrichment at the oxide/alloy interface during oxidation.
Lower-reactive-element HEAs will form thicker, less uniform, more defective oxide scales with faster oxidation kinetics.
The proposed behavior applies to single-phase HEAs under oxidizing conditions from 800 to 1200 °C.
The behavior may not extend to multiphase alloys or to other temperature and atmosphere regimes.
The threshold Cr/Al concentration needed for effective segregation is not yet determined.
